title: Vitals Integration Recipes
text: common pattern: optimize training data, evaluate held-test data.
code: # Full dataset with ground truth qa_data <- tibble(   question = c(     "What is the capital of France?",     "Who wrote Romeo and Juliet?",     "What is 2 + 2?",     "What color is the sky?",     "Who painted the Mona Lisa?",     "What is the largest planet?"   ),   target = c(     "Paris",     "Shakespeare",     "4",     "Blue",     "Leonardo da Vinci",     "Jupiter"   ) )  # Split into train/test set.seed(42) train_idx <- sample(nrow(qa_data), 4) trainset <- qa_data[train_idx, ] testset <- qa_data[-train_idx, ]  # Create and optimize module qa_module <- signature("question -> answer") |>   module()  # Optimize with few-shot examples from training set optimized <- compile(   LabeledFewShot(k = 2L),   qa_module,   trainset = trainset )  # Evaluate on held-out test set eval_task <- as_vitals_task(   module = optimized,   dataset = testset,   scorer = detect_match(),   name = "qa-test",   dir = tempdir(),   .llm = chat_openai(model = "gpt-4o-mini") )  eval_task$eval() #> ℹ Solving #> ✔ Solving [335ms] #>  #> ℹ Scoring #> ✔ Scoring [49ms] #>   # Compare performance cat("Test accuracy:", mean(eval_task$get_samples()$score == "C"), "\n") #> Test accuracy: 1

text: Test different module configurations side--side:
code: # Same signature, different approaches sig <- signature("question -> answer")  # Variant 1: Basic prediction basic <- module(sig)  # Variant 2: Chain-of-thought reasoning cot <- module(sig, type = "chain_of_thought")  # Test dataset test_data <- tibble(   question = c(     "If a train travels 60 mph for 2 hours, how far does it go?",     "What is 15% of 80?"   ),   target = c("120 miles", "12") )  llm <- chat_openai(model = "gpt-4o-mini")  # Evaluate both results <- list() for (name in c("basic", "cot")) {   mod <- if (name == "basic") basic else cot    task <- as_vitals_task(     module = mod,     dataset = test_data,     scorer = model_graded_qa(),     name = paste0("math-", name),     dir = tempdir(),     .llm = llm   )   task$eval()    results[[name]] <- mean(task$get_samples()$score == "C") } #> ℹ Solving #> ✔ Solving [338ms] #>  #> ℹ Scoring #> ✔ Scoring [283ms] #>  #> ℹ Solving #> ✔ Solving [339ms] #>  #> ℹ Scoring #> ✔ Scoring [290ms] #>   # Compare cat("Basic accuracy:", scales::percent(results$basic), "\n") #> Basic accuracy: 100% cat("CoT accuracy:", scales::percent(results$cot), "\n") #> CoT accuracy: 100%

text: complex evaluation logic, build custom pipeline:
code: # Custom evaluation function evaluate_module <- function(module, dataset, llm, scorer = detect_match()) {   # Run predictions   predictions <- run(     module,     !!!as.list(dataset[, -which(names(dataset) == "target")]),     .llm = llm   )    # Combine with targets   results <- tibble(     input = dataset$input,     target = dataset$target,     prediction = predictions[[1]] # First output column   )    # Score   results$correct <- results$prediction == results$target    # Summary   list(     accuracy = mean(results$correct),     n = nrow(results),     failures = results[!results$correct, ],     all = results   ) }  # Use it results <- evaluate_module(   module = sentiment_module,   dataset = test_data,   llm = chat_openai() )  cat("Accuracy:", scales::percent(results$accuracy), "\n") cat("Failures:", nrow(results$failures), "\n")

title: COPRO Teleprompter — COPRO
text: COPRO (Coordinate Prompt Optimization) automatically refines module instructions using coordinate ascent. iteration, generates multiple candidate instruction variants selects best performing one baseline next iteration. optimizer: Starts current module instructions baseline depth iteration: Generates breadth candidate instruction variants using prompt_model Evaluates candidate validation set Selects best performing instruction Uses best baseline next iteration Returns module optimized instructions

title: KNNFewShot Teleprompter — KNNFewShot
text: teleprompter uses k-nearest neighbor retrieval dynamically select demonstrations runtime based similarity input query. Unlike LabeledFewShot selects static demos compile time, KNNFewShot selects different demos query based embedding similarity.

title: KNNFewShot Teleprompter — KNNFewShot
text: metric metric function evaluating predictions. NULL, uses exact_match() default. metric_threshold Minimum score required considered successful. NULL, uses metric's default threshold. max_errors Maximum number errors allowed optimization. Default 5. k Number nearest neighbors use demonstrations. Default 3. vectorizer function takes character vector returns numeric matrix embeddings (one row per input). Required. input_text function converts training example (data frame row) character string embedding. Default concatenates input columns. cache_embeddings Whether cache embeddings training set. Default TRUE. merge_demos TRUE, merge KNN-selected demos existing demos module. Default FALSE (replace).

title: KNNFewShot Teleprompter — KNNFewShot
text: KNNFewShot works : Pre-computing embeddings training examples compile time runtime, embedding input query Finding k similar training examples using cosine similarity Using examples demonstrations current query approach particularly effective : training set large diverse Different types queries benefit different demonstrations Semantic similarity good proxy task relevance

code: # Create multiple compiled modules sig <- signature("question -> answer") mod1 <- module(sig, type = "predict") mod2 <- module(sig, type = "predict") mod3 <- module(sig, type = "predict")  # Combine with majority voting ens <- ensemble(list(mod1, mod2, mod3))  # With weighted voting based on validation scores ens <- ensemble(   list(mod1, mod2, mod3),   reduce_fn = reduce_weighted_vote(),   weights = c(0.9, 0.85, 0.8) )  # With custom reduce function custom_reduce <- function(outputs, weights = NULL) {   # Take the longest answer   lengths <- vapply(outputs, function(o) nchar(o$answer %||% ""), integer(1))   outputs[[which.max(lengths)]] } ens <- ensemble(list(mod1, mod2, mod3), reduce_fn = custom_reduce)
